sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:175889
Court No. - 66
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 40913 of 2024

Applicant :- Rakesh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Ashish Kumar Srivastava,Sr. Advocate
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Shiv Nath Singh, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Ashish Kumar Srivastava,
learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Kunwar Tejendra Bahadur, learned AGA, for the State.
2. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No. 133 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B, 301 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Badalpur, District Gautam Buddh Nagar during pendency of the trial.
3.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is father in law of deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture he has been made accused in the present matter along with his son i.e., husband of deceased.

4. He further submits that there is no allegation of demand of dowry in the FIR of the present case and however, when the statement of the informant was recorded during investigation, then he started making allegation that deceased was tortured due to demand of Rs. 4 lakh for buying a car Rakesh vs State Of U.P. on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5021547/
1 and this fact clearly suggest that subsequently during investigation, informant developed the story with regard to demand of dowry and actually it is not a case of dowry death.
5.
He further submits that it appears that some matrimonial dispute arose between husband and wife and thereafter his wife i.e., deceased committed suicide by hanging herself.

6. He next submits that immediately after the incident, applicant not only informed the police but he also informed the informant side and these facts are evident even from the FIR and the inquest report.
7.
He further submits that even the post-mortem report of the deceased also suggest that deceased died due to hanging.

8. He further submits that there is no specific allegation against applicant and he is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 16.05.2024, i.e., for the last more than five months.

9. Per contra, learned AGA, however, opposed the prayer for bail and submits that daughter in law of applicant died within five years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and there was also allegation of demand of dowry but could not dispute the fact that applicant is father in law of deceased and there is no specific allegation against him.

10. Learned AGA further could not dispute the fact that in the FIR, there is no allegation of demand of dowry, however, he pointed out that when the statement of informant was recorded during investigation, then he disclosed specific demand of dowry.
11. He further could not dispute the fact that on the information given by applicant, inquest was conducted and deceased died due to hanging.
12. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

13. However, daughter in law of applicant died within five years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but applicant is father in law of deceased and there is no specific allegation against him.

14. Further, in the FIR there was no allegation of demand of dowry and the post-mortem report suggest that deceased died due to hanging, therefore, prima facie it appears to be a case of suicidal death.
15. Further, record also suggest that after the incident applicant informed the informant and also to the police and on his information, inquest was conducted.
16. Further, applicant is not having any previous criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 16.05.2024, i.e., for the last more than five months.

Rakesh vs State Of U.P. on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5021547/
2 17.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
18. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant-Rakesh be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
20. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

21. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 8.11.2024 #Vik/-
